name: Dr Brendan Cronin

summary: Dr Brendan Cronin is a Corneal and Refractive Surgeon at the Queensland Eye Institute.
meta_description: Dr Brendan Cronin is a Corneal and Anterior Segment Surgeon and the Director of Education at the Queensland Eye Institute.
bio_html:
Dr Brendan Cronin is a Corneal and Refractive Surgeon at the Queensland Eye Institute.

Dr Cronin grew up on the Gold Coast and completed his medical training at the University of Queensland Medical School in Brisbane. He has international experience have trained in his subspecialty of Corneal, Refractive and Anterior Segment Surgery at the prestigious Manchester Royal Eye Hospital in the United Kingdom. He performs all types of corneal transplant surgery, pterygium surgery, cataract surgery and refractive surgery.  Dr Cronin has a special interest in keratoconus especially LASER “Athen’s Protocol” corneal regularisation combined with collagen cross-linking and Corneal Allogenic Intrastromal Ring Segments or “CAIRS”.  Together with Dr David Gunn, he developed www.cairsplan.com.  This pioneering website is used by surgeons globally to both learn the CAIRS procedure and to plan their surgical procedures.

Dr Cronin is regularly invited to speak at conferences internationally, has published articles in numerous international ophthalmology journals, has written two textbooks, holds international patents in corneal cross lining technology and is a member of The European Society of Cataract and Refractive Surgery, The Cornea Society, The Refractive Surgery Alliance, is a founding fellow of the World college of Refractive Surgery and Visual Sciences and is a fellow of the Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Ophthalmology.

When he isn’t at work Dr Cronin enjoys spending time with his wife and 2 daughters.

Pioneer of CAIRS keratoplasty in Australia

Dr Cronin has published more than 40 articles in international peer-reviewed journals including Ophthalmology, Cornea and the Journal of Cataract and Refractive Surgery, holds international patents for corneal collagen cross-linking technology and is a principal investigator on multiple international clinical trials. He was among the first surgeons in Australia to perform CAIRS keratoplasty, performed the world's first combined Bowman's membrane and CAIRS procedure, and successfully led the campaign for Medicare Australia to recognise CAIRS keratoplasty under item number 42653, making the surgery accessible to eligible Australians.

With Dr David Gunn he co-authored the Brisbane Nomogram, the world's first published standardised planning framework for CAIRS surgery (Clinical and Experimental Ophthalmology, 2026), and co-developed CAIRSPlan.com, the free online planning tool used by corneal surgeons across many countries. He performs refractive and therapeutic laser surgery through QEI Laser, with all surgery performed at South Brisbane Day Hospital.
treats: Micro-incision cataract surgery and lens replacement surgery, including multifocal lenses
All types of corneal transplant surgery including DMEK, DALK (including femtosecond laser assisted DALK) and penetrating keratoplasty
Keratoconus surgery including the laser "Athens protocol" (corneal resurfacing combined with collagen cross-linking) and CAIRS
Collagen cross-linking with Australia’s most advanced pupil-tracking topography-guided cross-linking machine
Therapeutic excimer laser (PTK) for corneal scarring, dystrophies, recurrent erosions and irregular astigmatism
LASIK, TransPRK, PRK, ASA and CLEAR laser eye surgery
